Primary Assets: ASSET-003 Customer PII; ASSET-004 Billing Records; ASSET-005 Customer Invoices; ASSET-014 API Authorization Logic
Rationale: An authenticated customer may manipulate predictable object identifiers and request records belonging to other customers if the application does not consistently enforce server-side ownership checks. Exploitation could potentially be repeated across many customer objects and expose PII, billing records, and invoices at scale.

Threat Name: Sensitive Data Exposure From Cloud Blob Storage
Primary Assets: ASSET-003 Customer PII; ASSET-005 Customer Invoices; ASSET-011 Cloud Blob Storage Content
Rationale: A cloud storage misconfiguration, overly permissive role assignment, or exposed access token could allow unauthorized users to retrieve customer invoices, reports, or other stored documents without passing through normal application authorization controls. Existing encryption and application-controlled access reduce likelihood, but storage permissions and access-token configuration remain realistic sources of exposure.

Affected Components: Administrator; Admin Portal; API Gateway; Application Server; Customer Data and Configuration

Rationale: A compromised administrator identity could allow an attacker to impersonate a trusted privileged user and perform sensitive account, access, recovery, and security-management operations. Existing MFA and Conditional Access reduce exposure, but privileged accounts remain high-value targets for phishing, session theft, and endpoint compromise.

STRIDE Category: Information Disclosure / Spoofing / Elevation of Privilege
Affected Components: Application Server; Customer Database; Payment API; Email Service; Cloud Resources
Primary Assets: ASSET-009 Application Secrets; ASSET-016 Third-Party API Credentials; ASSET-010 Customer Database; ASSET-003 Customer PII
Rationale: Application and third-party credentials may be exposed through source code, configuration files, logs, repositories, build artifacts, or compromised application systems. Without dedicated secrets management, automated scanning, rotation, and short-lived credentials, exposure remains realistically likely. A compromised secret could allow an attacker to impersonate a trusted application or service identity.

Affected Components: Application Server; API Gateway; Identity Systems; Monitoring and Logging Platform
Primary Assets: ASSET-012 Audit Logs; ASSET-013 Monitoring and Alerting Capability
Rationale: An attacker with sufficient access to production systems or logging infrastructure may attempt to modify or delete authentication, application, API, administrative, or security records in order to conceal malicious activity. Without immutable storage, separated logging privileges, tamper detection, and independent archival copies, log manipulation remains plausible.

Rationale: A compromised payment provider or stolen integration credential could allow an attacker to impersonate a trusted external service and provide manipulated transaction information to Northstar. Successful exploitation could result in fraudulent transaction state, billing-record manipulation, financial loss, customer disputes, and potentially disclosure of payment-related data.

Rationale: The customer portal and API are publicly accessible and therefore exposed to high-volume request activity from untrusted sources. Existing API Gateway, rate-limiting, monitoring, and cloud controls provide some protection, but without guaranteed DDoS mitigation, autoscaling, request-cost controls, circuit breakers, and downstream resource protection, application or database capacity could still be exhausted.

STRIDE Category: Tampering / Information Disclosure / Elevation of Privilege
Affected Components: Customer Browser; Web Front End; API Gateway; Application Server; Customer Database
Primary Assets: ASSET-003 Customer PII; ASSET-004 Billing Records; ASSET-010 Customer Database; ASSET-014 API Authorization Logic
Rationale: Customer-controlled input may reach database operations through the application layer. If queries are not consistently parameterized and database permissions are broader than required, crafted input could alter intended query behavior. Successful exploitation could disclose or alter large volumes of customer PII, billing records, and application data and could potentially disrupt core application operations.

Affected Components: Customer Database; Application Data; Backup Infrastructure
Primary Assets: ASSET-017 Backup and Recovery Data; ASSET-010 Customer Database; Business Continuity
Rationale: An attacker with sufficient access to backup infrastructure could delete, encrypt, or corrupt recovery data in order to weaken the organization's ability to recover from a later destructive event. Without immutable or offline copies, isolated backup identities, deletion protection, and tested recovery procedures, backup destruction remains realistically possible.

Affected Components: Web Front End; API Gateway; Application Server; Authorization Data
Primary Assets: ASSET-014 API Authorization Logic; ASSET-003 Customer PII; ASSET-010 Customer Database; ASSET-015 Application Source and Configuration
Rationale: A user may manipulate application requests or authorization data to assign themselves or another account privileges beyond the intended role. Without consistent server-side authorization, reauthentication, approval workflows, and protected privilege-change logging, unauthorized role modification remains plausible and could grant broad administrative capabilities.

Rationale: Compromise of the external email provider or its API credentials could allow an attacker to impersonate Northstar, alter customer communications, distribute phishing content, or suppress legitimate security and account notifications.
